solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novel features in this store?

parts.note: read 'novel' as a work of fiction rather than 'new': a shop whose stock is made up of fiction and other volumes

explanation.definitionFit: A retail outlet selling printed volumes, novels included, is exactly this kind of shop.

clue.text: Red weapon discovered finally in NW town

indicators.note: in places the weapon and the final letter inside the name of the town

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, north-west England
a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word discovered

explanation.surface: A red-coloured weapon is found at the end of a search in a north-western town.
explanation.walkthrough: BURY, a town near Manchester in north-west England, holds GUN plus D, the last letter of 'discovered', signalled by 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is a deep purplish-red colour, named after the wine.

clue.text: Place of refreshment, old, unaltered

parts.note: something left unaltered stays 'as is'

explanation.surface: A café or watering hole that is old and hasn't been changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert offers water and rest, so it is a place where travellers refresh themselves.

clue.text: Vegetable being munched could make boy sane

indicators.note: munched suggests chewed up and mangled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating a certain vegetable might restore a boy's sanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'munched' is the anagram signal on BOY SANE; 'being' and 'could make' just link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is a legume eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Miss offering love to tiny boy when upset

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the small boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A young lady offers her affection to a small lad who is feeling sad.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in A Christmas Carol; 'when upset' turns TIM into MIT below the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something out is to leave it out, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Karl's drug

definitions.meaning: Karl ... was the Austrian-British philosopher of science
slang for an amyl nitrite capsule inhaled as a recreational drug

explanation.surface: A man named Karl owns some narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the philosopher's surname and the slang term for an inhaled nitrite stimulant share the spelling.

clue.text: Month given to work in an organisation with widespread influence

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
an opus is a creative work, especially in music

explanation.surface: Someone is assigned for a month to a job in a large institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an octopus is a powerful body whose many arms reach everywhere.

clue.text: After various sprees, university fellow got on with it

indicators.note: after places the academic behind the reworked letters
various suggests differing versions, so the letters of sprees are rearranged

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Following several binges, an academic carried on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a charade signal, not a time word: the academic follows the jumbled sprees, with 'various' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to continue determinedly, so the past tense means carried on.

clue.text: Some of the army team found in lodge

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are one part of the British Army
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Part of a military squad is discovered staying in a hunting lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to dwell or live there, used as a verb.

clue.text: Giving a makeover to girly nest in need of renovation

indicators.note: renovation means remaking, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A girl's cosy home that needs doing up is getting a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyling something gives it a new look, which is what a makeover does.

clue.text: Horticultarists must get across lake? They sound angry

indicators.note: the gardeners stretch across the letter for lake, so it sits inside them

parts.note: gardeners who raise plants are growers

explanation.surface: Gardeners have to cross a lake, apparently making a furious noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get across' puts L inside GROWERS. The clue misspells horticulturists as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs or people who growl make a low angry noise, so these are snarlers.

clue.text: Garment very French worn by women

indicators.note: the French word wraps round the letter for women as clothing wraps round a body

parts.note: très is French for very

explanation.surface: A very French piece of clothing worn by ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: TRES (French for 'very') goes round W; 'worn by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Fifty in University Street meeting the Queen in the province

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral within the university-street pair

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone aged fifty on a university street encounters the monarch in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen. In British usage 'the province' means Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the historic Irish province, and 'the Province' is a common British name for Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Wrote music that's calm

definitions.meaning: a composer who wrote a piece created it

explanation.surface: Someone created a score that is soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means created a musical work, and the adjective means self-possessed and serene.

clue.text: Germany has smashing fat food

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
ripping is old-fashioned British slang for excellent, as is smashing

explanation.surface: Germany boasts some superb fatty cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' and 'ripping' are both dated British slang for splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is the fat that runs from roasting meat, eaten on bread in Britain.

clue.text: Trade declines unfortunately out of London?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Business sadly drops off, perhaps because it has moved away from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges TRADE DECLINES. The definition is an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Functions moved away from the capital to the regions have been devolved from the centre, illustrated here by London.

clue.text: Child like Venus in Paris lacking any social skills?

parts.note: the Venus de Milo statue in the Louvre in Paris has no arms

explanation.surface: A little one resembling a goddess in France is socially awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo, displayed in the Louvre, has lost both arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without charm lacks the personal appeal that eases social dealings.

clue.text: Pile of muck creates delay in phase of redevelopment

indicators.note: in places the word for delay within the reworked letters
redevelopment suggests rebuilding, so the letters of phase are rearranged

parts.note: a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: Muck piles up because there is a hold-up in a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of redevelopment' reads as building talk, but 'redevelopment' is the anagram signal; 'creates' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is a mound of mining waste, literally a pile of dirt and spoil.

clue.text: Like certain weapons sent in plane or distributed some other way

indicators.note: spreading things out in a different arrangement signals that the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Arms might be dispatched by aircraft or handed out by another method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed some other way' rearranges SENT IN PLANE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipersonnel weapons such as landmines target people rather than vehicles, so the word describes a class of arms.

clue.text: Person providing the property, he having departed?

definitions.text: Person providing the property, he having departed?

parts.words: Person providing the property, he having departed?
parts.note: describes someone who has died after making a will that passes on his estate

explanation.definitionFit: In law the word describes, or as a noun names, a person who has died leaving a valid will.

clue.text: Writer getting terribly sore about certain batsmen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the writing tool
terribly suggests badly done, so the letters of sore are scrambled

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An author grows very angry about some cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen in; 'terribly' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the opening pair are the two batsmen who start the innings.

clue.text: Minor insult

explanation.surface: A small affront.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means trivial, and the noun means a slur or snub.

clue.text: Hide from essayist's relations

parts.note: Charles Lamb was the English essayist who wrote as Elia
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself from a writer's family members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for an animal's skin. Charles Lamb was a famous English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, and this is the skin of a young sheep.

clue.text: Sailor travels west with commercial cargo

indicators.note: cargo is goods held inside a vessel, so the advert sits within the turned word
in an across clue, moving west means reading from right to left

parts.note: goes means travels
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A seaman heads westward carrying merchant goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west' reverses the verb in an across clue, and 'cargo' puts the advert inside the turned word, as goods sit in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sea dog is an experienced sailor.

clue.text: Day on river? That is right — it's raining less!

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A day on the river is fine, as the rain is easing.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain eases, conditions become less wet, the comparative of dry.

clue.text: Wise fellows can give one a leg up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gam is slang for a leg
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Clever men can offer someone a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM is slang for leg; 'up' turns it into MAG, followed by I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the three wise men who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Girl is terrific but ultimately getting a bit twisted

indicators.note: only the closing stretch of the word is turned round, a bit at the end swapped

parts.note: great means terrific

explanation.surface: A young woman is wonderful, though in the end she becomes somewhat devious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately getting a bit twisted' turns only the final AT of GREAT into TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a girl's name, as in the actress Greta Garbo.

clue.text: Unofficial information may be given on this plant

definitions.text: Unofficial information may be given on this plant

parts.words: Unofficial information may be given on this plant
parts.note: gossip is said to be heard 'on' a certain climbing plant, and the clue also names the plant itself

explanation.definitionFit: Rumour spreads 'on the grapevine', and the grapevine is also the climbing plant bearing grapes.

clue.text: Dispute's terrible — this examiner makes an appearance

indicators.note: the answer shows itself among the letters of the words dispute's terrible

explanation.surface: An argument is dreadful, and now an inspector turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes an appearance' signals the hidden run inside dispuTES TERrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester examines or checks something, making the two words synonyms.

clue.text: Side on journey given somewhere to land

parts.note: side means affected airs, as in putting on side
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Getting on a trip, someone is offered a landing place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is the old British sense of pretentiousness, like airs.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft land.
